title: Needle-felted bullfinch
subtitle: A round-bodied male bullfinch in rose-pink, black, and grey merino
excerpt: Needle felt a male bullfinch with its vivid rose-pink breast, jet-black cap and bib, grey back, and white rump. The round compact body is about 6 cm beak to tail and sits naturally on a flat base.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from traditional British needle-felting guild practice. Garden bird forms are among the most popular beginner needle-felting subjects in the UK.

glossaryTerms.definition: A dry felting method using barbed needles to lock wool fibres together without heat or water.
Wool drawn into a continuous ribbon; the standard input material for needle-felting work.

content.text: is four clean colour blocks on a round, stout body: rose-pink breast, jet-black cap and bib, blue-grey back, and white rump. The colours meet in definite lines with no blending, which makes it one of the more satisfying British garden birds to lay up: the finished piece looks crisp rather than muddy. Use firm
in each colour and needle each section cleanly before moving to the next.

attrs.title: Needle safety
attrs.body: Stab straight in and out at 90 degrees. Keep the finger guard in place on the supporting hand.

items.name: Black merino roving (cap, bib, wings edge, tail)
White merino roving (rump patch, wing bar)
Strong thread and needle for bead eyes

content.text: Roll the grey roving into a compact round-oval body about 5.5 cm long. Needle felt on all sides until the form is firm. The bullfinch body is notably round, fuller at the breast than most garden birds, so keep the core compact and resist elongating it. The tail end narrows slightly; taper the rear of the body as you work.

Apply rose-pink roving across the entire front face of the body, from just below where the cap will sit down to the belly, covering roughly the lower front half. Needle the edges so the pink meets the grey in a clean curve across each shoulder and straight down each flank. The breast colour should be strong and even, not streaky.
Step 3: Build the head and black cap

Roll a small grey ball for the head base and attach it to the body. Apply black roving over the entire top and back of the head down to the base of the bill, and across the throat and bib down to the top of the breast. The black bib and cap are continuous in the bullfinch, not two separate patches; keep the coverage complete. Shape a short, rounded bill from black roving and needle it to the front of the face.
Step 4: White rump and wing details

Needle a white oval patch at the rump (between the grey back and the tail base). This white rump is a field-mark distinctive to the bullfinch and lifts the finished piece considerably; do not skip it. Add a thin white line across the wing as a wing bar, then needle two flat black tail feathers at the rear of the body.

Stitch the bead eyes into the black face area, just to the sides of the bill, pulling them tight so they sit close to the surface. The eyes are set low in the face in bullfinches, just above the bib line. Trim any surface fibres with small scissors and check that all colour boundaries are clean.

items.problem: The pink breast looks dull or grey-tinged
items.cause: Grey fibres from the core body pulled through the pink surface layer during needling
items.fix: Apply a second thicker layer of pink roving over the breast and needle it in firmly. Keep the needle strokes shallow or grey fibres will pull up from the core.

items.problem: The black cap and bib look patchy
items.cause: The black roving layer was too thin, letting the grey or pink show through
items.fix: Apply black roving in short, overlapping tufts and needle each one down thoroughly before adding the next. Multiple thin layers build a more even surface than one thick layer.
